key_insight: The paper adds a single, system-level confidence score to multiagent debate by calibrating raw confidence signals and aggregating them with soft voting or Bayesian fusion.
engineering_relevance: This enables multiagent NLP systems to expose more useful uncertainty for oversight, downstream decision-making, and reliability monitoring without hurting answer quality.
method: Transform confidence scores so outputs from different models become comparable.
Aggregate calibrated confidences using soft voting or Bayesian fusion.
Compare sequence-probability and self-report estimators with parametric and non-parametric calibration.
evidence_signal: Across six homogeneous and heterogeneous debating pairs on five benchmarks and four task types, the aggregated confidence was more discriminative than the best single agent or standard MAD baselines, while F1 stayed stable.
watch_item: The approach depends on calibration quality and may behave differently across model pairs and ambiguous tasks, so implementation should validate calibration separately for each setup.
paper_title: Multiagent Protocols with Aggregated Confidence Signals
